messages.content:
The record:
Write the postmortem for the incident below.

Alert: CachedSpendTotalsAreStale on io-shop
What the alert said [AL1]: 90 {A1} of 240 {A2} cached spend figures disagree with the purchases behind them. The purchases are correct and the cached copies are behind: the widest gap is 88.46 {A3}, the most any one figure is missing is 1 {A4} purchase, and the oldest purchase none of them account for was recorded at 2026-11-10T23:11:00Z {A5}, which is when the copies stopped keeping up, and they were being served from 2026-11-11T02:04:08Z {A6}. Discarding the entries listed will send those pages back to the purchase ledger, which never moved. The list is what disagreed when this check ran: nothing is putting the copies right, so a figure goes stale as soon as its shopper buys again and a later check will name more.
Alert raised: 2026-11-11T02:09:53Z {alert_raised}
Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one. An alert rule fires; a person is paged. Argus first posted about the incident in Slack at 2026-11-11T02:09:57Z {first_told}, and the document says so already: leave that post out, and do not say that no person was told. That nobody was paged is a finding of its own.
The alert rule fires as soon as its condition holds. The alert came 5 minutes 45 seconds {alerted_after_the_onset} after the onset.
Broken from 2026-11-11T02:04:08Z {began} (the onset). The service was not back to normal by 2026-11-11T02:10:24Z {argus_stopped}, so it was broken for at least 6 minutes 16 seconds {duration} - a lower bound, not a measurement, and every impact figure below is bounded the same way.
Argus held the incident for 30 seconds {held}, until 2026-11-11T02:10:24Z {argus_stopped}. That is not how long the fault lasted, nor how long Argus went on working - leave it out of your answer.
Error rate: not measured by the metrics - the metrics for the incident could not be read.
Customer loss: none so far - the shop's takings over the incident fell short of the same hours whole weeks earlier by no more than those hours vary on their own, if at all; a lower bound, counted with the service not seen back to normal.

What Argus did, in order:
  - [T1] 2026-11-11T02:09:53Z {T1.1} Argus: Received CachedSpendTotalsAreStale on io-shop
  - [T2] 2026-11-11T02:10:02Z {T2.1} Argus: Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up
  - [T3] 2026-11-11T02:10:02Z {T3.1} Argus: Called in the Investigator Agent
  - [T4] 2026-11-11T02:10:08Z {T4.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's per-minute metrics, anchored on 02:09:53 {T4.2}
  - [T5] 2026-11-11T02:10:11Z {T5.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 0 {T5.2} minutes of metrics
  - [T6] 2026-11-11T02:10:11Z {T6.1} Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 02:04 {T6.2}
  - [T7] 2026-11-11T02:10:12Z {T7.1} Investigator Agent: Recorded where the 3 {T7.2} replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB
  - [T8] 2026-11-11T02:10:12Z {T8.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 {T8.2} day 5 {T8.3} minutes 45 {T8.4} seconds before Nov 11 02:09:53 {T8.5}
  - [T9] 2026-11-11T02:10:13Z {T9.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 0 {T9.2} production changes
  - [T10] 2026-11-11T02:10:13Z {T10.1} Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 {T10.2} replicas run one revision, which the history does not name
  - [T11] 2026-11-11T02:10:14Z {T11.1} Investigator Agent: Read the service register - the service calls io-pricing (internal, owned by checkout-platform), io-summary-cache (internal, owned by checkout-platform), io-pay (third-party, owned by IO Payments Ltd)
  - [T12] 2026-11-11T02:10:14Z {T12.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's log lines, the 3 {T12.2} hours before Nov 11 02:09:08 {T12.3}
  - [T13] 2026-11-11T02:10:15Z {T13.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 0 {T13.2} log lines
  - [T14] 2026-11-11T02:10:16Z {T14.1} Investigator Agent: Formed 2 {T14.2} candidate causes, best first: C1, C2
  - [T15] 2026-11-11T02:10:16Z {T15.1} Investigator Agent: Read every channel available
  - [T16] 2026-11-11T02:10:16Z {T16.1} Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 0 {T16.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 {T16.3} hour before 02:10:16 {T16.4}
  - [T17] 2026-11-11T02:10:20Z {T17.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATING to act on a candidate
  - [T18] 2026-11-11T02:10:20Z {T18.1} Argus: Called in the Mitigation Agent
  - [T19] 2026-11-11T02:10:22Z {T19.1} Mitigation Agent: Discarded the stale cached figures of io-shop for C1
  - [T20] 2026-11-11T02:10:23Z {T20.1} Mitigation Agent: Judged the action CONFIRMED
  - [T21] 2026-11-11T02:10:24Z {T21.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATED - discarded [90 {T21.2}] of [io-shop]'s stale cached figures and the store reported what it removed, which is the whole of what was wrong
  - [T22] 2026-11-11T02:12:25Z {T22.1} Code-Fix Agent: Proposed a fix as a draft pull request - https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/526

Changes to production it read:
  - Deploys read, none came back; flags read, none came back.

Log lines it read, one per message:
  - Read; none came back.

Candidates it considered, in the Investigator's words - name them by their labels, but cite none; what they claim is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [C1, also C2] Candidates blaming the same move of io-summary-cache, each reading it as a different kind of failure - different accounts of what it did, not one cause counted twice - each in its own words:
      C1: The cached spend totals (io-summary-cache) stopped keeping up with the purchase ledger from 2026-11-10T23:11:00Z {C1.1} and began being served stale at 2026-11-11T02:04:08Z {C1.2}. The ledger is right and only the derived copy is behind. No deploy, config change or rollout is recorded. [state-divergence, confidence 0.75 {C1.3}, confirmed]
      C2: The internal cache service io-summary-cache, owned by checkout-platform, is failing to apply updates and so serves stale spend figures. [internal-dependency-failure, confidence 0.15 {C1.4}, confirmed, as tested for C1]

Actions it took:
  - [M1] Discarded the stale cached figures of io-shop for [C1] - confirmed, nothing to put back

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix, and what it claims is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [F1] The fault: in `src/io_shop/account_page.py`, `_the_figure_for` asks the cache first. If `cached_summary` returns an entry, it returns `found.amount_cents` as the page's figure and does no other check. According to `src/io_shop/summary_cache.py`, each entry stores two things: the figure, and `items_counted`, the number of purchases the figure was worked out from. The page already has the shopper's `Account` and its purchases in hand. But it never compares the two, so once whatever keeps the cache up to date stops, every entry it can read is shown as current. This is the failure the investigation describes: the purchase ledger is correct and the cached copy is behind, so shoppers saw stale figures. `src/io_shop/cache_reconciliation.py` treats a mismatch in `items_counted` as a sign of a stale entry, but only in an offline check, never on the serving path.
      
      The fix: `_the_figure_for` now uses a cached entry only if `found.items_counted == len(account.purchases)`. If the counts differ, it falls through to `render_spend_summary`, the same path a cache miss already takes. So a stale entry costs one recomputation instead of a wrong figure. Checking the count is just the length of a tuple already in memory, so the cache still saves the walk through the purchase history. Nothing about the cache being unreachable changes. That case is still reported in `cache_failure` and does not fail the page. With no cache configured, the page behaves as before.
      
      Tests (`tests/io_shop/test_account_page.py`): the `a_cache_holding` helper now takes the purchase count the entry claims. The existing "served from cache" test now uses an entry that matches its 2-purchase account; it previously claimed 8 {F1.1} purchases, which is exactly the mismatch this change rejects. A new test gives the page an entry that is one purchase short. It asserts that the page shows the figure worked out from the purchases (2000 {F1.2}), not the cached 999 {F1.3}, and that `served_from_cache` is False. Against the current code, that test would get 999 {F1.4} from the cache.
  - Say what the files Code-Fix read do, with the conditions it gives - a default as a default, never as all it does - and no wider: 'nothing in the files it read', never 'nothing in the code'.

Action items the record already holds:
  - AI-1 (mitigate, done): Discarded the stale cached figures of io-shop
  - AI-2 (mitigate, open): Review and merge the proposed fix
PR #526 is a draft Argus opened for a person to review and merge. The record holds nothing about it after that: do not say it was reviewed, approved or merged, or that it was not - nor that the record holds nothing, which the document says itself. Nothing ran its test or its fix: say what it proposes, not that it corrects anything.

Cite evidence in causal_chain by its label. In a contributing factor's addressed_by, name the record's own action items that answer it, by their number; an item you propose names the factors it answers in its answers, by their labels.

Call submit_postmortem with your answer.

The document, by field:
root_cause: From {A5} the cached spend totals stopped being updated as new purchases were recorded, so the cached copies fell behind the purchase ledger, which stayed correct, and account pages were served those copies from {A6}. The evidence does not show what stopped the updates.
cause_in_plain_words: The saved copies of shoppers' spending totals stopped being updated when new purchases came in, and the account pages likely showed those copies without checking them against the purchases; what stopped the updates is not known.
still_at_risk: Nothing was keeping the cached spend figures up to date, so any shopper's figure could go stale again with their next purchase and be shown on their account page.
symptom: Shoppers' account pages showed spend totals that were behind their purchases
causal_chain 1: Shoppers' account pages showed spend totals that did not match the purchases behind them. (cites AL1)
causal_chain 2: The pages took their spend figures from cached copies that had fallen behind the purchase ledger. The ledger itself was correct and never moved, and only the cached copies were wrong. (cites AL1; T21, under "What Argus did, in order")
causal_chain 3: From {A5} the cached copies stopped keeping up with new purchases, and nothing was putting them right. The record does not show what stopped the updates, and no change was found that set this off. (cites AL1)
contributing_factors 1: Code-Fix read the account page's code in src/io_shop/account_page.py. In that reading, when the cache returns an entry, the page shows that entry's figure without comparing the purchase count stored with it to the shopper's purchases, which the page already has in hand. In the files Code-Fix read, the only check that treats a count mismatch as a sign of a stale entry is an offline reconciliation check, not on the serving path.
contributing_factors 1 had_it_been_otherwise: Each stale entry would have been worked out again from the purchase ledger, so shoppers would have seen correct figures even though the cache had stopped keeping up.
contributing_factors 2: No alert was seen that would catch the cached spend figures no longer being updated. The fault was found only by the check comparing cached figures with the purchases behind them, after the stale copies were already being served.
contributing_factors 2 had_it_been_otherwise: The updates stopping at {A5} could have been caught and dealt with before stale figures were served to shoppers from {A6}.
action_items 1: Find what stopped the cached spend figures in io-summary-cache from being updated with new purchases from {A5}, and get those updates running again, working with checkout-platform, which owns io-summary-cache.
action_items 2: Add an alert that fires when the cached spend figures stop being updated with new purchases, separate from the check that compares the figures being served.
action_items 3: Link the CachedSpendTotalsAreStale alert to on-call so that a person is paged when it fires.
action_items 4: Find out why the investigation got no metrics and no log lines back for io-shop, and fix it.
went_well 1: The alert itself listed which cached figures disagreed and when the copies stopped keeping up, which gave the mitigation an exact list of entries to discard.
went_wrong 1: Nobody was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was asked to look into why the cached figures had stopped being updated.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {T5.1} or {duration}, are figures code writes in from the row they name. They are not judged.
  - Action items propose what to do; they make no claim about the record.
  - Whether something went well, went wrong or was lucky is a judgement. Only a fact it states is judged.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
